question.text: Are OCBs (Overseas Corporate Bodies) permitted to invest in Indian mutual funds?

answer.text: No, OCBs are prohibited from investing in Indian mutual funds
Yes, but only in debt schemes

explanation.text: The Logic: OCBs (Overseas Corporate Bodies) are prohibited from investing in Indian mutual funds. The RTA must screen for and reject any application received from an OCB. The Trap: Since FPIs (Foreign Portfolio Investors) and NRIs can invest, candidates may assume OCBs can also invest. They cannot — OCBs are a specifically excluded investor category. Note: If an entity claims to be an OCB, the application must be rejected. To invest in Indian mutual funds, a foreign entity would generally need to qualify under a permitted route such as FPI registration.
